title: Cluster Lifecycle with kubeadm, etcd and High Availability

header.html: Prepare underlying infrastructure for installing a Kubernetes cluster; Create and manage Kubernetes clusters using kubeadm; Manage the lifecycle of Kubernetes clusters; Implement and configure a highly-available control plane

toc.title: Prepare the infrastructure (Reference only, plus two checks you can run)
Create a cluster with kubeadm (Reference only)
Lifecycle: upgrade (Reference only) and node maintenance (executed)

html:
1Prepare the infrastructure (Reference only, plus two checks you can run)

Before kubeadm init every node needs:

Requirement Why Command
Swap off the kubelet does not run with swap on by default swapoff -a (and remove it from /etc/fstab)
Packet forwarding Pods route traffic through the node sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward must be 1
Bridge traffic seen by iptables Service rules apply to bridged traffic modules overlay and br_netfilter, sysctl net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables=1
A container runtime runs the containers containerd, with SystemdCgroup = true
Matching cgroup driver kubelet and runtime must agree kubelet cgroupDriver: systemd in /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml
kubeadm, kubelet, kubectl installed and held at one version the three must be compatible package manager, then apt-mark hold
Open ports API server 6443, etcd 2379-2380, kubelet 10250 firewall or security group

You can check two of these on a node (Lab 3.7). On the test nodes net.ipv4.ip_forward is 1 and the kubelet cgroupDriver is systemd.

2Create a cluster with kubeadm (Reference only)

On the first control plane node:

kubeadm init --pod-network-cidr=<cidr> --kubernetes-version=v1.37.0
mkdir -p ~/.kube && cp /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf ~/.kube/config
# install a CNI plugin by applying its manifest, then:
kubeadm token create --print-join-command        # run on a control plane node
kubeadm join <api>:6443 --token ... --discovery-token-ca-cert-hash sha256:...   # run on each worker
  • kubeadm init creates certificates in /etc/kubernetes/pki, kubeconfigs, static Pod manifests, and a bootstrap token.
  • A token lasts 24 hours by default; make a new one with kubeadm token create --print-join-command (executed in Lab 3.4). kubeadm token list shows them.
  • Without a CNI plugin the nodes stay NotReady and CoreDNS stays Pending.

3etcd backup and restore (executed)

etcd holds all cluster state. A snapshot is the backup. Find the connection details in the etcd static Pod manifest (/etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml): the listen address and the three certificate files.

ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 \
  --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt \
  --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt \
  --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key \
  snapshot save /opt/backup/etcd.db
etcdutl snapshot status /opt/backup/etcd.db -w table     # check it

Restore into a new data directory, then point the etcd Pod at it:

etcdutl snapshot restore /opt/backup/etcd.db --data-dir /var/lib/etcd-restore
vi /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml      # hostPath volume "etcd-data": path: /var/lib/etcd-restore

The kubelet restarts the etcd Pod when the manifest changes.

Finding from the lab, important: after a restore, the API server, controller manager and scheduler still hold caches from before the restore. In the test cluster the namespace controller stopped working (namespaces stuck in Terminating, log lines "is not as new as written version") until those three components were restarted. Restart them (move their manifests out of /etc/kubernetes/manifests, wait, move them back) and wait for the cluster to answer.

Notes for the exam:

  • etcdctl is installed on the exam hosts, and etcdutl may be needed for restore. On recent versions, etcdutl snapshot restore works on the file directly (no endpoints, no certificates).
  • Do the work on the control plane node named in the task (ssh <node>).
  • Always verify the backup file with snapshot status before declaring it done.

4Certificates

kubeadm leaf certificates are valid for one year by default (the test cluster shows 364 days left after one day); the CA certificates are valid for ten years according to the kubeadm documentation. Check them:

kubeadm certs check-expiration
openssl x509 -in /etc/kubernetes/pki/apiserver.crt -noout -enddate

Renew with kubeadm certs renew all (then restart the control plane Pods). Upgrading the cluster with kubeadm upgrade also renews certificates.

5Lifecycle: upgrade (Reference only) and node maintenance (executed)

Upgrade order (one minor version at a time, never skip a minor):

  1. Control plane node: upgrade the kubeadm package, kubeadm upgrade plan, kubeadm upgrade apply v1.X.Y.
  2. Drain the node, upgrade kubelet and kubectl, restart the kubelet, uncordon.
  3. Each other control plane node: kubeadm upgrade node.
  4. Each worker: drain, upgrade the kubeadm package, kubeadm upgrade node, upgrade kubelet, restart, uncordon.

Node maintenance (Lab 3.5):

Command Effect
kubectl cordon <node> marks it unschedulable; running Pods stay
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets cordons and evicts the Pods (DaemonSet Pods are skipped); needed for any node with workloads
kubectl uncordon <node> makes it schedulable again

drain refuses to evict Pods that use local storage (emptyDir) or are not managed by a controller unless you add --delete-emptydir-data or --force. Pods that belong to a Deployment are recreated on other nodes.

6High availability (concept; Reference only)

Topology etcd location Trade-off
Stacked etcd etcd runs on each control plane node simpler; losing a node loses a control plane member and an etcd member
External etcd separate etcd nodes more machines; control plane and etcd fail independently
  • Use an odd number of etcd members (3 or 5). A quorum (majority) must be up: 3 members tolerate 1 failure, 5 tolerate 2.
  • Put a load balancer in front of the API servers; kubeadm init --control-plane-endpoint=<lb>:6443 --upload-certs and kubeadm join ... --control-plane add more control plane nodes.
  • Scheduler and controller manager use leader election: only one is active at a time.
  • Workers need no change; they reach the API through the load balancer.

7Lab tasks

<!-- LABS: m03 -->

Lab 3.1: etcd backup

Domain: Architecture | Points: 7 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m03-01-etcd-backup)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

On the control plane node cka-control-plane, take a snapshot of etcd and save it as /opt/backup/etcd.db. Find the endpoint and the certificate paths in the etcd static Pod manifest. etcdctl is installed on the node.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

ssh cka-control-plane 'grep -E "cert-file|key-file|trusted-ca-file|listen-client" /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml'
ssh cka-control-plane 'etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key snapshot save /opt/backup/etcd.db'

Lab 3.2: etcd restore

Domain: Architecture | Points: 8 | Time: about 10 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m03-02-etcd-restore)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

A snapshot of etcd exists at /opt/backup/etcd-before.db on cka-control-plane. The namespace keep was deleted by mistake after that snapshot. Restore the cluster from the snapshot so that namespace keep exists again. Use the new data directory /var/lib/etcd-restore and make the etcd static Pod use it. The cluster must be healthy at the end: restart the control plane components that cache cluster state so that they pick up the restored data.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

ssh cka-control-plane 'etcdutl snapshot restore /opt/backup/etcd-before.db --data-dir /var/lib/etcd-restore'
ssh cka-control-plane 'sed -i "s#path: /var/lib/etcd\$#path: /var/lib/etcd-restore#" /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml; grep -n "path: /var/lib/etcd" /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml'
ssh cka-control-plane 'mkdir -p /tmp/off && mv /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-{apiserver,controller-manager,scheduler}.yaml /tmp/off/ && sleep 20 && mv /tmp/off/*.yaml /etc/kubernetes/manifests/'   # restart the control plane Pods so they drop stale caches
until kubectl get --raw /readyz >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 2; done
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready node --all --timeout=180s

Lab 3.3: cert expiry

Domain: Architecture | Points: 4 | Time: about 4 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m03-03-cert-expiry)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

On the control plane node, find the date on which the certificate of the API server (/etc/kubernetes/pki/apiserver.crt) expires. Write it exactly as OpenSSL prints the notAfter value (for example Nov 9 18:39:01 2027 GMT) to ~/answers/expiry.txt on the host.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

ssh cka-control-plane 'kubeadm certs check-expiration 2>/dev/null | grep -E "^apiserver "'
ssh cka-control-plane 'openssl x509 -in /etc/kubernetes/pki/apiserver.crt -noout -enddate' | cut -d= -f2 > ~/answers/expiry.txt

Lab 3.4: join command

Domain: Architecture | Points: 5 | Time: about 4 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m03-04-join-command)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

A new worker node must join the cluster. On the control plane node, create a new bootstrap token and save the complete kubeadm join command (with token and CA certificate hash) to ~/answers/join.txt on the host.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

ssh cka-control-plane 'kubeadm token create --print-join-command 2>/dev/null' > ~/answers/join.txt
cat ~/answers/join.txt

Lab 3.5: drain node

Domain: Architecture | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m03-05-drain-node)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Node cka-worker2 needs maintenance. Make it unschedulable and evict the workloads from it, leaving the DaemonSet Pods alone (Pods that use emptyDir volumes may be deleted). A Deployment web in the namespace maint (4 replicas) must still have all 4 replicas Ready afterwards, on the other nodes.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl drain cka-worker2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
kubectl -n maint rollout status deployment web --timeout=120s

Lab 3.6: etcd members

Domain: Architecture | Points: 4 | Time: about 4 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m03-06-etcd-members)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Using etcdctl on the control plane node, find the name of the etcd member (as shown by the member list) and write it to ~/answers/member.txt on the host.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

ssh cka-control-plane 'etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key member list -w simple'
ssh cka-control-plane 'etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key member list -w json' | python -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['members'][0]['name'])" > ~/answers/member.txt

Lab 3.7: node prereqs

Domain: Architecture | Points: 4 | Time: about 4 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m03-07-node-prereqs)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Before installing Kubernetes on a node you check two prerequisites on cka-worker. Write to ~/answers/prereq.txt two lines: line 1 is the value of the kernel setting net.ipv4.ip_forward (0 or 1), line 2 is the cgroup driver the kubelet is configured with (the cgroupDriver value in the kubelet configuration file).

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

ssh cka-worker 'sysctl -n net.ipv4.ip_forward' > ~/answers/prereq.txt
ssh cka-worker 'grep cgroupDriver /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml' | awk '{print $2}' >> ~/answers/prereq.txt

Lab 3.8: kubeadm config

Domain: Architecture | Points: 5 | Time: about 5 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m03-08-kubeadm-config)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

kubeadm stores the cluster configuration in a ConfigMap. Find the kubernetesVersion and the clusterName recorded in the ClusterConfiguration and write them to ~/answers/kubeadm.txt on the host, two lines: kubernetesVersion: <value> then clusterName: <value>.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n kube-system get configmap kubeadm-config -o jsonpath='{.data.ClusterConfiguration}' | grep -E "^(kubernetesVersion|clusterName):" | sort -r > ~/answers/kubeadm.txt
cat ~/answers/kubeadm.txt

<!-- /LABS -->

8Recall questions

R1Which flag of etcdctl snapshot save files must you take from the etcd manifest?

Show the answer

The endpoint and the CA, server certificate and server key paths (--cacert, --cert, --key).

R2After restoring etcd to a new directory, what must change so the cluster uses it?

Show the answer

The hostPath of the data volume in the etcd static Pod manifest.

R3Why restart the API server, controller manager and scheduler after a restore?

Show the answer

They hold caches from before the restore; stale caches break controllers (for example namespaces stay Terminating).

R4How do you get a new kubeadm join command after the first token expired?

Show the answer

kubeadm token create --print-join-command on a control plane node.

R5What is the difference between cordon and drain?

Show the answer

cordon only stops new scheduling; drain also evicts the existing Pods (use --ignore-daemonsets).

R6Can you upgrade from v1.35 to v1.37 in one step?

Show the answer

No; upgrade one minor version at a time.

R7How many etcd members tolerate one failure, and why odd numbers?

Show the answer

3. A majority (quorum) must stay up; an odd count gives the best fault tolerance for the size.

R8Which command lists certificate expiry dates on a kubeadm cluster?

Show the answer

kubeadm certs check-expiration.

Quick Reference Card

Topic Remember
Prepare nodes swap off, ip_forward=1, br_netfilter, containerd with systemd cgroups
Init / join kubeadm init, then CNI, kubeadm token create --print-join-command
etcd backup etcdctl snapshot save with --endpoints --cacert --cert --key; verify with etcdutl snapshot status
etcd restore etcdutl snapshot restore --data-dir <new>, edit manifest hostPath, restart control plane components
Certs kubeadm certs check-expiration, kubeadm certs renew
Maintenance cordon, drain --ignore-daemonsets, uncordon
Upgrade one minor at a time; control plane first; kubeadm upgrade plan/apply/node
HA odd etcd count, load balancer, stacked or external etcd, leader election
